newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian protesters battle police-two more dead.
newsitem.headline: Albanian protesters battle police-two more dead.

text.p: Two people died on Monday when demonstrators battled riot police in the Albanian port of Vlore, pinning them down in the main police station.
A duty nurse at Vlore hospital said a 30-year-old demonstrator had been shot and died after an operation. The second victim, a man of 51, died of heart failure before reaching hospital.
Dozens were injured, mostly by flying stones, in the clashes which brought to three the number of people killed in two days of trouble.
In Tirana, senior members of President Sali Berisha's ruling Democratic Party blamed the unrest on "terrorists" and unanimously backed the government's handling of the crisis.

"All measures are being taken to maintain public order and safeguard institutions," Genc Pollo, a member of parliament and spokesman for Berisha, told the official ATA news agency. "This is clearly terrorist activity."

Protesters drove back police in Vlore's central square where they had gathered peacefully for five days to denounce Berisha and demand the return of savings lost in collapsed pyramid investment schemes.
Protesters punched the air and shouted "Vlore is ours!" Some elderly women cowered and wept in rubble-strewn streets, others trampled captured police shields underfoot.
"We don't want a war, just our money," shouted one young man. "The police are fascists!" shrieked a middle-aged woman.

Demonstrators then dragged wrecked cars and oil drums through the streets to the police station, erected barricades and set them alight. Demonstrators and police remained locked in a stand-off by the building through most of the day.
"Police can only work here at night," shouted Xhemil, a ragged protester in his late teens. "During the day it's ours. Berisha is finished."
About 30 police crouching outside a cafe behind plastic shields endured first an onslaught of stones and then tables and chairs dropped from an overhead terrace.
Some officers surrendered and suffered the additional indignity of being ordered to strip off their uniforms, which were then thrown onto a bonfire. Others retreated to hills overlooking the town.

The Health Ministry said 26 people, policemen and protesters, remained in hospital with injuries and 55 were released after treatment. Fifteen policemen were transferred to a hospital in Tirana, 150 km (90 miles) to the north.
The director of Vlore hospital said many injuries were caused by plastic riot-control bullets.

The police station was the theatre for initial clashes on Sunday night, when protesters threw stones at the building and police fired into the air. One demonstrator died, officials said of a heart attack but demonstrators blamed the police.

Protesters accuse Berisha and his right-wing government of failing to warn investors of the pitfalls of pyramid schemes, which have attracted the savings of virtually every family in post-communist Albania. Economists estimate up to $2 billion may be tied up in the schemes altogether.
The opposition Forum for Democracy alliance renewed its calls for Berisha to replace his administration with a "technocrat government" to tackle the pyramid crisis.
It called a rally in a Tirana stadium on Wednesday. An opposition demonstration in the capital last weekend, banned by authorities, was broken up by riot police with truncheons.
Outside Vlore police station, shots periodically rang out and cars raced past to evacuate wounded protesters.
Officers perched on rooftops dropped chunks of concrete but never seemed to hit their targets. Bolder protesters threw stones at the building occasionally and retreated.
About 2,000 protesters also gathered in the southern town of Gjirokastra, joined by Albanians working in nearby Greece.

Unrest against the collapse of the schemes first erupted last month in Albania, Europe's poorest country. But a rash of arrests and the threat of long jail sentences had kept protesters off streets for a time.
